serialFormats.description: Legacy 10-character York serial (1971 - Oct 2004): four letters + six-digit sequence. Letter 1 = plant, letter 2 = month, letter 3 = year, letter 4 = item type (M = mfg. basic unit, P = purchased basic unit, S/T = low-side item, Y/Z = accessory). Year letters cycle every 21 years; this entry is the FIRST cycle (A = 1971 ... Y = 1991).
sources: York Serial Numbers ID - From History to October 2004 (York/UPG serial ID sheet, usair-eng.com/Serialnumber.pdf)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup (partstown.com/cm/resource-center/guides/gd2/york-serial-number-lookup)
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age (building-center.org/york-hvac-age/)
PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/york/)
How To Look At A House - age of a York air conditioner or furnace from the serial number (2018)
notes: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN: the year letter repeats every 21 years (A = 1971 or 1992 ... N = 1983 or 2004). The decoder will also match the 1992-2004 entry and flag the result ambiguous; pick the cycle from the nameplate: R-22 units with an ANSI/AHRI standard year printed on the plate in the 1990s, a Simplicity board, or a 10 SEER/EER rating are the 1992-2004 cycle; units this old (1971-1991) are rarely still in service.
Months skip I and J (K = Sep, L = Oct, M = Nov, N = Dec). Year letters skip I, O, Q, U.

Only ADFM654321 is a source-stated example (Parts Town / InspectApedia state it decodes to April, 1976 or 1997). The other two examples are rule-derived fixtures, not nameplate photos - which is why confidence is medium, not high.
The item-type letter (position 4) is captured as [A-Z]; the York sheet lists M, P, S, T, Y, Z. Coleman (Wichita, W) and Luxaire/Fraser-Johnston products built by York used this same scheme.

serialFormats.description: Legacy 10-character York serial (1971 - Oct 2004), SECOND letter cycle: year letter A = 1992 ... N = 2004. Same layout as the 1971-1991 entry: plant letter, month letter, year letter, item-type letter, six-digit sequence.
sources: York Serial Numbers ID - From History to October 2004 (York/UPG serial ID sheet, usair-eng.com/Serialnumber.pdf)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age
PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age: Serial Number Decoding
How To Look At A House - age of a York heat pump from the serial number (2020): letter series repeated every 21 years
notes: Regex only admits year letters A-N (1992-2004); letters P-Y in position 3 can only be 1984-1991 and are handled by the 1971-1991 entry, so those serials decode unambiguously.

For A-N the 1971-1983 cycle also matches: disambiguate from the nameplate (R-22 Sunline 2000 / Predator D-series with a Simplicity board = this cycle). The format ended in October 2004 (last letter N = 2004).
ADFM654321 is the source-stated example (April 1997 in this cycle); NLNM123456 and WGJM000789 are rule-derived fixtures.

serialFormats.description: Current York / Coleman / Luxaire / Fraser-Johnston / Champion serial (October 2004 - present): letter, digit, letter, digit, six-digit sequence (e.g. W1G7123456). Position 1 = plant, positions 2 and 4 read together = year (1 + 7 = 2017), position 3 = month letter (A-H = Jan-Aug, K = Sep, L = Oct, M = Nov, N = Dec).
sources: PICKHVAC - York HVAC Age (example W1G7123456 = July 2017, Wichita)
Building Intelligence Center - York HVAC age (2nd and 4th positions = year, 3rd = month letter, used exclusively since 2004)
Parts Town - York Serial Number Lookup
Central Air Conditioner and Refrigeration - How to read York HVAC model and serial number (examples W0E4298223 = 2004, W1E0298223 = 2010)
How To Look At A House - York heat pump age (2020): W1D5... = 2015
York Central Tech Talk - How To Read York Serial Numbers (2011, distributor 'decoder ring' PDF)
notes: Year = (digit in position 2) x 10 + (digit in position 4), 2000-based: W1G7 = 2017, N2K3 = 2023, W0E4 = 2004. Pattern letter/digit/letter/digit cannot be confused with the four-letter legacy format.
Month letters skip I and J (K = Sep). Several third-party decoders describe this as 'A to N, skipping I and J' - the same map.
Nameplate: York/JCI plates print 'SERIAL NO.' directly under 'MODEL NO.'; Coleman, Luxaire, Fraser-Johnston and Champion plates use the identical scheme (all built by JCI Unitary Products).

Confidence is medium (many agreeing secondary decoders; the first three examples are source-stated, N2K3456789 is a rule-derived fixture). No manufacturer document or warranty lookup could be consulted in this session - a JCI warranty lookup on york.com would raise it to high.
Rumoured newer formats (e.g. 'S...E...' 2019+) could not be confirmed; 'S' as position 1 is the Source 1 parts plant code in this same format.

controls.name: York Simplicity / Simplicity LITE unit control board (UCB) LED flash codes
controls.description: Single-LED flash-code diagnostics on the York unit control board. Original Simplicity (Sunline 2000 / Predator D-series, ~1998-2009: LAST ERROR button, Modbus/BAS port, fault history) and Simplicity LITE (Z-series 3-12.5 t, ~2009-2015) use different flash tables; only states confirmed from a cited source are listed here. Enrichment pass (2026-09-26) added no codes: no manufacturer document or corroborating source could be retrieved during the pass, and the verification protocol forbids transcribing codes from memory. The flash-code list here remains limited to the four states cited from ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 and one secondary thread; for any other flash count, or for Simplicity SE / Elite alarm and history codes (SE-MOBILE app or display), read the flash-code / alarm table printed on the unit's control-box label or in the unit IOM (e.g. 5188244-YIM, 826081-XIM) before acting. Enrichment pass 2026-09-26 (search-only; WebFetch blocked). Flash codes were read from search summaries of the York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66, ZJ078/ZF150 Sun Pro IOM p.60, Predator BP120 IOM p.40, Sunline DCG IOM p.55 and DUQ024-060 IOM p.28; meanings are transcribed as the summaries quoted them and should be spot-checked against the printed tables by a verifier. Coverage is 'partial': the UCB flash table (steady/heartbeat/off, 1-14) and ICB flash table (heartbeat, 1-10) are believed complete for original Simplicity and Simplicity LITE (the DM090 IOM table also ends at 14 flashes), b

faultCodes.meaning: On Steady - Control Failure - Replace Control
likelyCauses: Failed unit control board processor
Board not booting (check 24 VAC supply and board fuse before condemning)
checks: Verify 24 VAC at the board R-C terminals and check the board fuse
Cycle 24 V control power once; York Central Tech Talk: a steady-on LED (or one that never lights with power applied) that does not clear after a power cycle means the board must be replaced
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('On Steady - Control Failure - Replace Control'); same row in Predator BP120 IOM p.40 and ZJ078 IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: Heart Beat - Normal Operation
checks: No active fault; the ZE036 IOM describes normal operation as a 1 second on / 1 second off heartbeat, while fault codes flash at about 200 ms on / 200 ms off
If the unit is not responding, check the thermostat inputs (Y1/Y2/W1/W2/G) at the board and the ASCD timer (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('Heart Beat - Normal Operation')

faultCodes.meaning: 2 Flashes - Control waiting ASCD
likelyCauses: Anti-short-cycle delay (ASCD) timer running after a compressor stop or power-up
Call for cooling arrived before the minimum off time expired
checks: Wait out the ASCD (typically a few minutes) and confirm the compressor starts
Verify the Y call is still present at the board; a code that never clears while Y is present indicates a board or input problem (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('2 Flashes - Control waiting ASCD'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40; ZJ078 IOM p.60
faultCodes.notes: The manual's condition text for this code was not fully visible in the search summary; causes are interpretive.

faultCodes.meaning: 10 Flashes - Compressors Locked Out On Low Outdoor Air Temperature
likelyCauses: Outdoor ambient below the low-ambient switch setpoint (York Central Tech Talk: the low ambient switch is normally open, closes at about 45 F and opens at about 55 F)
Failed/shorted low ambient switch or wiring, or low-ambient switch installed where a low-ambient kit is not fitted
checks: Measure outdoor ambient; above about 55 F the switch should be open - ohm it and its wiring to the UCB
If the unit must cool at low ambient, confirm a low-ambient kit is installed and the switch is wired per the kit instructions (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('10 Flashes - Compressors Locked Out On Low Outdoor Air Temperature'); York Central Tech Talk 'Simplicity Diagnostics Flash Codes' (FC 10); ZJ078 IOM p.60
faultCodes.notes: LOW confidence - from a secondary source only; confirm against the flash-code table printed on the unit's control-box label or IOM.

faultCodes.meaning: OFF - No Power or Control Failure
likelyCauses: No 24 VAC to the board (open transformer, blown board fuse, tripped breaker, open safety in the 24 V feed)
Failed unit control board
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the board power terminals; check the control transformer secondary and the board fuse
With good 24 VAC and no LED after a power cycle, replace the UCB (York Central Tech Talk: an LED that does not light at all with power applied indicates a possibly defective board)
faultCodes.source: York ZJ078 Sun Pro IOM 'Unit Control Board Flash Codes' p.60 ('OFF - No Power or Control Failure'); York Central Tech Talk 'Simplicity Diagnostics Flash Codes'

faultCodes.meaning: 1 Flash - Not Applicable
likelyCauses: Not a defined fault on this board
checks: Re-count the flashes; a single flash is not used as a code (the ICB table states a 1-flash code is not used to prevent confusion)
If the LED truly shows one flash between pauses, treat the board as suspect and confirm the flash pattern printed on the control-box label
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('1 Flash - Not Applicable'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40

faultCodes.meaning: 3 Flashes - HPS1 - Compressor Lock out
likelyCauses: High pressure switch on circuit 1 opened (dirty condenser coil, failed condenser fan motor, overcharge, non-condensables, restricted liquid line)

Open HPS1 wiring or a failed switch (the HVAC-Talk 'York Rooftop Alarm Codes' case showed a 3-flash lockout in winter with the switch closed and the unit tied to a BAS - check the board input and any BAS-written lockout)
checks: Read head pressure on circuit 1 and compare with the HPS trip rating on the unit label; check condenser coil cleanliness and condenser fan operation
Ohm HPS1 and its wiring back to the board input with the circuit at rest; the switch should be closed
Clear the lockout by removing the thermostat call or cycling 24 V power after correcting the cause (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('3 Flashes - HPS1 - Compressor Lock out'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40 ('HPS1 Compressor Lockout'); ZJ078 IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: 4 Flashes - HPS2 Compressor Lockout
likelyCauses: High pressure switch on circuit 2 opened (dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, liquid-line restriction)
Open HPS2 wiring or failed switch
checks: Read circuit 2 head pressure and compare with the HPS rating; inspect condenser coil and fan
Ohm HPS2 and its wiring to the board with the circuit at rest
Clear by removing the call or cycling 24 V power once the cause is corrected (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Predator BP120 IOM p.40 'Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('4 Flashes - HPS2 Compressor Lockout'); York ZJ078 Sun Pro IOM p.60 (same row); not present on single-compressor ZE036 table

faultCodes.meaning: 5 Flashes - LPS1 - Compressor Lock out
likelyCauses: Low pressure switch on circuit 1 opened (low charge / leak, restricted metering device or filter drier, low indoor airflow, low ambient without low-ambient controls)
Open LPS1 wiring or failed switch
checks: Check circuit 1 suction pressure against the LPS rating; verify charge by superheat/subcooling and check for leaks
Verify indoor airflow (filters, blower, coil) and evaporator condition
Ohm LPS1 and wiring to the board input; clear by removing the call or cycling 24 V power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('5 Flashes - LPS1 - Compressor Lock out'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40 ('LPS1 Compressor Lockout'); ZJ078 IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: 6 Flashes - LPS2 Compressor Lockout
likelyCauses: Low pressure switch on circuit 2 opened (low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, low ambient)
Open LPS2 wiring or failed switch
checks: Check circuit 2 suction pressure against the LPS rating; verify charge and look for leaks
Verify indoor airflow and evaporator condition
Ohm LPS2 and wiring to the board input; clear by removing the call or cycling 24 V power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Predator BP120 IOM p.40 'Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('6 Flashes - LPS2 Compressor Lockout'); two-compressor Sun Pro (ZJ078/ZF150 IOM p.60) carries the same row
faultCodes.notes: One search summary of the ZJ078 p.60 table appeared to list LPS2 at 7 flashes; the Predator BP120 table read explicitly (6 = LPS2, 7 = FS1) and the ZE036 table (5 = LPS1, 7 = FS1) support this numbering. Confirm against the flash-code label in the unit control box.

faultCodes.meaning: 7 Flashes - FS1 - Compressor Lock out
likelyCauses: Freeze stat (FS1) on evaporator circuit 1 opened - coil running too cold: low indoor airflow (dirty filters, iced coil, blower problem), low charge, or low return-air temperature
Open FS1 wiring or failed freeze stat; on some units a lockout with a warm coil points to a wiring/board input problem
checks: Inspect the evaporator for ice; check filters, blower speed/belt and external static (GHAC: code 7 = Compressor 1 Freezestat open)
Verify circuit 1 charge and suction saturation temperature; a low charge drives the coil below freezing
Ohm FS1 and its wiring at the board with the coil thawed; the switch should be closed
Clear by removing the call or cycling 24 V power after the coil has thawed and the cause is corrected (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('7 Flashes - FS1 - Compressor Lock out'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40 ('FS1 Compressor Lockout'); GHAC 'Predator - Flashing Code 7' (secondary corroboration)

faultCodes.meaning: 8 Flashes - FS2 Compressor Lockout
likelyCauses: Freeze stat (FS2) on evaporator circuit 2 opened - low airflow, low charge or low return-air temperature
Open FS2 wiring or failed freeze stat
checks: Inspect the evaporator for ice; check filters, blower and external static
Verify circuit 2 charge and suction saturation temperature
Ohm FS2 and its wiring at the board with the coil thawed; clear by removing the call or cycling 24 V power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Predator BP120 IOM p.40 'Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('8 Flashes - FS2 Compressor Lockout'); two-compressor Sun Pro (ZJ078/ZF150 IOM p.60) carries the same row

faultCodes.meaning: 9 Flashes - Ignition Control Locked Out / Ignition Control Failure / Limit Switch Trip / No Jumper Plug in Heat Section
likelyCauses: Ignition control board (ICB) in lockout after repeated ignition failures (no gas, weak flame signal, dirty flame sensor, bad igniter, pressure switch)
Limit switch or rollout switch open, or the heat-section jumper plug missing on a cooling-only unit

York Central Tech Talk: five separate conditions can cause FC 9; read the ICB LED to tell which. A contactor coil with high resistance can drop board voltage and also trigger a 9 (HVAC-Talk 9-flash thread)
checks: Go to the ignition control board and read its own flash code (see the 'ICB ...' codes in this table) before touching the UCB
Check the limit and rollout switches for continuity; verify the heat-section jumper plug is installed on units without gas heat
Check gas pressure, flame-sensor microamps and igniter; clean the flame sensor
Clear the ICB lockout by removing the W call or cycling power after the cause is corrected (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('9 Flashes - Ignition Control Locked Out/Ignition Control Failure/Limit Switch Trip/No Jumper Plug in Heat Section'); Predator BP120 IOM p.40 ('Ignition Control Locked Out / Ignition Control Failure'); York Central Tech Talk 'Simplicity Diagnostics Flash Codes'

faultCodes.meaning: 11 Flashes - Compressors Locked Out Because The Economizer Is Using Free Cooling
likelyCauses: Normal: economizer is in free-cooling mode and the board is holding the compressors off (York Central Tech Talk: on units shipped with a factory economizer the switch is set ON, so compressors are locked out while the economizer is in free cooling)
Economizer wrongly signalling free cooling (enthalpy/changeover setting, failed economizer control, wiring) while outdoor conditions are not suitable
checks: Check the economizer changeover setting and outdoor conditions; if free cooling is not appropriate, check the economizer control and its free-cooling signal to the UCB
On units with no economizer, verify the board economizer option switch / jumper is set correctly
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('11 Flashes - Compressors Locked Out Because The Economizer Is Using Free Cooling'); York Central Tech Talk (FC 11); ZJ078 IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: 12 Flashes - Unit Locked Out due to Fan Overload Switch Failure
likelyCauses: Supply fan motor overload tripped (belt-drive units): high amps from overloaded blower, wrong pulley setting, failed bearings, or a failed overload relay
York Central Tech Talk: FC 12 indicates 24 VAC is not detected on the Fan Over terminal - open overload contact, wiring, or missing jumper on units without an overload
checks: Check the supply fan motor overload for a trip; measure fan motor amps against nameplate and check pulley setting / external static
Verify 24 VAC at the board Fan Over(load) terminal; on units without an overload confirm the factory jumper is in place
Reset the overload and clear the lockout by cycling 24 V power after correcting the cause (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZF150 / ZJ078 Sun Pro IOM p.60 'Unit Control Board Flash Codes' ('12 Flashes - Unit Locked Out due to Fan Overload Switch Failure'); York Central Tech Talk (FC 12 - Fan Overload Lockout)
faultCodes.notes: Not listed on the single-compressor 3-5 t ZE036 table (direct-drive blower, no overload).

faultCodes.meaning: 13 Flashes - Compressor Held Off Due To Low Voltage
likelyCauses: Low 24 VAC at the board - York Central Tech Talk: the control sensed less than about 19.2 VAC while attempting to energize a relay, or less than about 16 VAC with relays already energized; it is an information code, not a lockout
Undersized or failing control transformer, overloaded 24 V circuit (extra relays, economizer, thermostat), high-resistance contactor coils, low line voltage or loose connections
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the board with the compressor contactor(s) pulling in; look for the dip below ~19 V
Check line voltage and the transformer tap, then the total 24 V load (contactor coils, economizer, accessories) and connections
Ohm the contactor coils - a high-resistance coil drops board voltage (HVAC-Talk 9-flash thread)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('13 Flashes - Compressor Held Off Due To Low Voltage'); York Central Tech Talk (FC 13); ZJ078 IOM p.60

faultCodes.meaning: 14 Flashes - EEPROM Storage Failure (Control Failure)
likelyCauses: Internal board memory (EEPROM) fault - York Central Tech Talk: an internal control fault; if it does not reset after cycling power the board must be replaced
Electrical noise / power event corrupting stored settings
checks: Cycle power to the board once; if 14 flashes returns, replace the UCB
Check for a poor ground or a failing transformer before fitting the new board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 ('14 Flashes - EEPROM Storage Failure (Control Failure)'); York Central Tech Talk (FC 14 - EPROM failure)

faultCodes.meaning: Heart Beat - Normal Operation (ignition control board)
checks: ICB is healthy; if there is no heat, check the W call reaching the ICB, gas supply and the UCB flash code
faultCodes.source: York ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes'; York Sunline DCG IOM p.55; DUQ024-060 IOM p.28

faultCodes.meaning: 1 Flash - Not Applicable (a 1-flash code is not used to prevent confusion)
likelyCauses: Not a defined ICB code
checks: Re-count the flashes between pauses
faultCodes.source: York Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('1 Flash - Not Applicable'; note that a 1-flash code is not used to prevent confusion)

faultCodes.meaning: 2 Flashes - Pressure / Centrifugal Switch Open With Inducer On
likelyCauses: Inducer (combustion blower) running but the pressure switch has not closed: blocked or restricted flue / vent, blocked pressure-switch tubing, weak inducer motor, failed pressure switch, wind or condensate in the switch line
On centrifugal-switch designs, the inducer is not reaching speed or the centrifugal switch has failed
checks: Confirm the inducer runs; measure pressure-switch draw with a manometer and compare with the switch rating
Inspect the flue, vent terminal, heat exchanger outlet and switch tubing for blockage or water
Jumper the switch only as a test to confirm the switch vs the draw
faultCodes.source: York Sunline DCG IOM p.55 / DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('2 Flashes - Pressure/Centrifugal Switch Open With Inducer On'); same table in ZE036 IOM p.66

faultCodes.meaning: 3 Flashes - Pressure / Centrifugal Switch Closed With Inducer Off
likelyCauses: Pressure switch stuck closed or contacts welded
Miswired pressure-switch circuit, or a jumper left on the switch terminals
checks: With the inducer off, ohm the pressure switch - it should be open; replace if closed
Check for a test jumper left on the switch terminals and for wiring shorts
faultCodes.source: York Sunline DCG IOM p.55 / DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('3 Flashes - Pressure/Centrifugal Switch Closed With Inducer Off')

faultCodes.meaning: 4 Flashes - Not Applicable
likelyCauses: Not a defined ICB code on this table
checks: Re-count the flashes; confirm against the ICB label
faultCodes.source: York Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('4 Flashes - Not Applicable')

faultCodes.meaning: 5 Flashes - Lock Out From Too Many Flame Losses
likelyCauses: Flame established then lost repeatedly: dirty or cracked flame sensor, poor ground, low gas pressure, flame lifting off the burners, burner carryover problems, unstable draft
Gas valve dropping out or low supply pressure under load
checks: Clean the flame sensor and measure flame current; check burner ground and the sensor lead
Check manifold and inlet gas pressure with all burners lit; check burner alignment and carryover
Reset by removing the W call or cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Sunline DCG IOM p.55 / DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('5 Flashes - Lock Out From Too Many Flame Losses')

faultCodes.meaning: 6 Flashes - High Temperature Switch Open
likelyCauses: High-limit switch open: low airflow across the heat exchanger (dirty filters, blower or belt problem, closed dampers, high static), overfired burners, or a failed limit
Blower not running during heat (blower delay, motor)
checks: Check filters, blower operation, belt, and temperature rise against the nameplate range
Check manifold pressure / firing rate; ohm the limit switch when cool
Repeated limit trips also lock out the UCB with 9 flashes - clear both after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 / Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('6 Flashes - High Temperature Switch Open')

faultCodes.meaning: 7 Flashes - Rollout Switch Open
likelyCauses: Flame rollout switch tripped (manual reset): restricted heat exchanger or flue, cracked heat exchanger, blocked burners, inducer/venting problem, delayed ignition
Open rollout wiring
checks: Do not simply reset: inspect the heat exchanger, burners and flue for the cause of rollout before returning the unit to service
Check for delayed ignition (gas pressure, igniter position, burner carryover)
Reset the rollout switch(es) and ohm the circuit after the cause is corrected
faultCodes.source: York DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 / Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('7 Flashes - Rollout Switch Open')

faultCodes.meaning: 8 Flashes - Flame Present With Gas Off
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through or stuck open
Flame-sense circuit falsely detecting flame (shorted sensor lead, moisture, board fault)
checks: Close the manual gas valve and see if the code clears; check for burner flame with the valve de-energized - replace a leaking gas valve
Inspect the flame sensor lead for shorts to ground and moisture on the board
faultCodes.source: York DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 / Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('8 Flashes - Flame Present With Gas Off')

faultCodes.meaning: 9 Flashes - Gas Valve Stuck OFF or ON
likelyCauses: ICB sees the gas valve output state disagreeing with the flame / valve feedback: failed gas valve coil, open valve wiring, or a valve stuck open
Low 24 V at the valve or a failed ICB relay
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the gas valve terminals during the trial for ignition; check inlet/manifold pressure
Check the valve wiring and coil resistance; replace the valve if it fails to open or close
faultCodes.source: York DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 / Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('9 Flashes - Gas Valve Stuck OFF or ON')

faultCodes.meaning: 10 Flashes - Flame Sense Circuit Failure
likelyCauses: Internal ICB flame-sense circuit fault
Shorted / grounded flame sensor lead
checks: Inspect the flame sensor and lead for shorts to ground; cycle power
If the code returns with a good sensor and lead, replace the ignition control board
faultCodes.source: York DUQ024-060 IOM p.28 / Sunline DCG IOM p.55 'Ignition Control Board Flash Codes' ('10 Flashes - Flame Sense Circuit Failure')

faultCodes.code: SE: C1 Locked Out Due to High Pressure
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm - C1 Locked Out Due to High Pressure: three HPS1 trips within two hours (same alarm exists as C2/C3/C4 for HPS2/HPS3/HPS4)
likelyCauses: High pressure switch trips on the named compressor: dirty or blocked condenser coil, condenser fan / ECM fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, liquid-line restriction, high ambient recirculation
Intermittent HPS wiring or a weak switch
checks: Open Details > Alarms (or the SE-MOBILE / MAP view) and note which circuit and how many trips
Check head pressure against the HPS rating, condenser coil, condenser fan operation and charge
Hard lockouts are cleared by cycling power or via the ResetLO parameter (see diagnostic tips); York states high pressure lockout occurs after 3 trips in 2 hours
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix - Critical alarms ('C1 Locked Out Due to High Pressure - Three HPS1 trips within two hours' ... C4/HPS4); York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later' (high pressure lockout after 3 trips in 2 hours)

faultCodes.code: SE: C2 Locked Out Due to High Pressure
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm - C2 Locked Out Due to High Pressure: three HPS2 trips within two hours
likelyCauses: High pressure switch trips on compressor 2: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
Intermittent HPS2 wiring or a weak switch
checks: Check circuit 2 head pressure, condenser coil and fan, and charge
Clear the hard lockout by cycling power or via ResetLO after repair
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix - Critical alarms ('C2 Locked Out Due to High Pressure - Three HPS2 trips within two hours')

faultCodes.code: SE: C1 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm - C1 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure: three LPS1 trips within one hour (same alarm exists as C2/C3/C4 for LPS2/LPS3/LPS4)
likelyCauses: Low pressure switch trips on the named compressor: low charge / leak, restricted filter drier or TXV, low indoor airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient operation without low-ambient control
Intermittent LPS wiring or a weak switch
checks: Check suction pressure and superheat/subcooling on the named circuit; look for leaks
Check indoor airflow (filters, blower, coil) and evaporator icing
York states low pressure lockout occurs after 3 trips in 1 hour; clear by cycling power or via ResetLO after repair
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix - Critical alarms ('C1 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure - Three LPS1 trips within one hour' ... C4/LPS4); York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later'

faultCodes.code: SE: C2 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm - C2 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure: three LPS2 trips within one hour
likelyCauses: Low pressure switch trips on compressor 2: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient
Intermittent LPS2 wiring or a weak switch
checks: Check circuit 2 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling and airflow
Clear the hard lockout by cycling power or via ResetLO after repair
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix - Critical alarms ('C2 Locked Out Due to Low Pressure - Three LPS2 trips within one hour')

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor locked out on evaporator coil freeze: York states coil freeze lockout occurs after 3 trips in 2 hours (the SE sequence takes protective action when an evaporator coil sensor EC1-EC4 reads below 42 F; freezestat alarm documented under Unit protection)
likelyCauses: Evaporator coil running too cold: low indoor airflow (filters, blower, VFD/IntelliSpeed setting, high static), low charge, low return-air temperature or economizer bringing in cold air with cooling on
Failed or miswired evaporator coil temperature sensor (EC1-EC4) or freezestat
checks: Read the evaporator coil sensor values in Details/Summary > Sensors and compare with the actual coil temperature; check sensor resistance if the reading is wrong
Check filters, blower operation and airflow setting; verify charge by superheat/subcooling
Clear the hard lockout by cycling power or via ResetLO after the coil has thawed and the cause is corrected
faultCodes.source: York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later' ('Coil freeze lockout occurs after 3 trips in 2 hours'); Smart Equipment Controls Sequence of Operation LIT-12011950 'Unit protection - Evaporator coil freeze condition' and 'Freezestat alarm'
faultCodes.notes: The exact alarm string shown on the display was not visible in the sources; the lockout rule and the coil-freeze protection are from the manufacturer documents.

faultCodes.meaning: Heat locked out on limit switch trips: York states limit switch lockout occurs after 3 trips in 1 hour (three LS1, LS2 or LS3 trips within one hour trigger a limit switch lockout)
likelyCauses: High-limit trips on the named heat section: low airflow across the heat exchanger (dirty filters, blower / VFD setting, closed dampers, high static), overfiring, blower delay or failure
Failed or loose limit switch wiring
checks: Check filters, blower and heating airflow setting; measure temperature rise against the nameplate range
Check manifold pressure / firing rate; ohm the limit switch when cool
Clear the hard lockout by cycling power or via ResetLO after repair
faultCodes.source: York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later' ('Limit switch lockout occurs after 3 trips in 1 hour'); York Smart Equipment Control Troubleshooting Guide 6138895-UTG (three LS1, LS2 or LS3 trips within one hour)

faultCodes.meaning: Heat locked out on air (pressure) switch trips: York states air pressure switch (APS) lockout occurs after 3 trips in 1.5 hours (three APS trips within 1.5 hours triggers a lockout alarm)
likelyCauses: Combustion air pressure switch not proving with the inducer running: blocked flue / vent, blocked or wet switch tubing, weak inducer, failed switch, wind
Switch closing intermittently during the heat cycle
checks: Measure pressure-switch draw with a manometer against the switch rating; inspect the flue, vent and switch tubing
Check the inducer motor and wheel; check the switch contacts
Clear the hard lockout by cycling power or via ResetLO after repair
faultCodes.source: York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later' ('Air pressure switch (APS) lockout occurs after 3 trips in 1.5 hours'); York Smart Equipment Control Troubleshooting Guide 6138895-UTG

faultCodes.code: SE: Unit Shutdown Due to Smoke
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm - Unit Shutdown Due to Smoke (the SD/24V shutdown input opened: smoke detector, condensate overflow and/or user shutdown relay wired in series)
likelyCauses: Duct smoke detector tripped (smoke, dirty detector, or a detector needing reset)
Condensate overflow switch or a field shutdown contact in the same series loop opened; open wiring in the SD loop
checks: Check the smoke detector status and reset it if tripped after the cause is cleared; check the condensate pan / overflow switch
Verify 24 VAC returns to the board shutdown input through the series loop (SD-24 is the 24 VAC hot out for smoke detector, condensate overflow and/or user shutdown relay switching in series)
The unit restarts when the input closes; power cycle if it remains latched (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 alarm list ('Unit Shutdown Due to Smoke'); Johnson Controls J ZB Series IOM 'Smart Equipment Unit Control Board' (SD-24 description); LIT-12011950 'Unit protection - Condensate Overflow Switch'

faultCodes.meaning: Service alarm - Economizer board goes from Online to Offline (SA bus communication with the economizer controller lost)
likelyCauses: SA bus wiring / connector fault between the UCB and the SE-ECO economizer controller
Economizer controller unpowered or failed; wrong SA bus address / duplicate device
checks: Check the green SA Bus LED on the UCB (flashing = communicating with SA bus devices; steady = awaiting communication)
Check SA bus cable, connectors and 24 V at the economizer board; confirm the board shows as Online under the device/commissioning menu
Cycle power and re-run device discovery if the board was replaced (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix - Service alarms ('Economizer board goes from Online to Offline'); Smart Equipment Quick Start Guide (SA Bus LED behavior)

faultCodes.code: SE FDD: Air temperature sensor failure
faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 economizer FDD - Air temperature sensor failure/fault: 'Problem with one of the air temperature sensors. Check Outdoor Air, Return Air, or Supply Air sensors.'
likelyCauses: Open, shorted or out-of-range OAT, RAT or SAT sensor; damaged sensor lead
Sensor unplugged after service
checks: Read OAT/RAT/SAT in the controller sensor menu; a reading at the range limit points to the failed sensor
Ohm the suspect 10k thermistor against a thermometer reading and check its wiring/connector
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 2 Title 24 FDD codes; NS Series Network Sensors with Fault Code Capability instructions 24-10094-76 (same code text)

faultCodes.code: SE FDD: Not economizing when it should
faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 economizer FDD - Not economizing when it should: 'The economizer is not using outdoor air when it should.'
likelyCauses: Damper actuator not opening (failed actuator, linkage, no signal), economizer disabled or changeover setpoint too low
Failed OAT / enthalpy sensor making the controller think outdoor air is unsuitable
checks: Compare OAT/RAT readings and the changeover setting with actual conditions; command the damper open from the controller and watch it move
Check actuator power and signal, linkage and damper blades
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 2 Title 24 FDD codes; NS Series Network Sensors instructions 24-10094-76

faultCodes.code: SE FDD: Economizing when it should not
faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 economizer FDD - Economizing when it should not (economizer using outdoor air when conditions do not permit)
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open or actuator failed open; changeover setpoint too high
Failed OAT / enthalpy sensor reading falsely cool
checks: Check the damper position against the commanded position; check the actuator and linkage
Verify OAT/enthalpy sensor readings and the changeover setting
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 2 Title 24 FDD codes ('Economizing when it should not')

faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 economizer FDD - Damper not modulating: 'The economizer damper is not able to modulate properly. Check damper, linkage to actuator, or the actuator.'
likelyCauses: Failed or unpowered actuator, broken or slipping linkage, damper blades seized or obstructed
Loss of feedback / control signal to the actuator
checks: Command the damper through its range from the controller and watch the blades; check actuator power, signal and feedback
Free and lubricate the damper and linkage; replace the actuator if it does not track the signal
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 2 Title 24 FDD codes; NS Series Network Sensors instructions 24-10094-76

faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 economizer FDD - Excess outdoor air: 'The economizer is allowing excess outdoor air inside.'
likelyCauses: Damper not closing to the minimum position (actuator, linkage, minimum position set too high)
Damper blades or seals damaged; return damper stuck
checks: Check the minimum position setting and the damper's actual closed position; inspect blades and seals
Check the actuator and linkage for full travel to the closed stop
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 2 Title 24 FDD codes; NS Series Network Sensors instructions 24-10094-76

faultCodes.meaning: Refrigeration circuit FDD - Recover Charge: higher than expected subcooling indicates the system may have more refrigerant charge than expected; consider recovering refrigerant
likelyCauses: Circuit overcharged (charged by weight without accounting for line length, or topped off on a hot day)
Condenser airflow restriction or a failed pressure/temperature sensor giving a false subcooling reading
checks: Verify subcooling with gauges and a clamp thermometer against the unit charging chart before recovering refrigerant
Check condenser coil and fan; check the FDD board's pressure and temperature sensors if the calculated subcooling disagrees with gauges
faultCodes.source: Simplicity SE (Smart Equipment) Controls Technical Guide 5127914-UTG Table 3 refrigeration circuit FDDs ('Recover Charge' - higher than expected subcooling)
faultCodes.notes: Only this one Table 3 entry was readable in search results; the FDD board reports other charge/efficiency/capacity diagnostics that are not transcribed here.

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 1 locked out due to excessive high pressure switch trips
likelyCauses: Repeated HPS1 trips: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
Intermittent HPS1 wiring
checks: Check circuit 1 head pressure, condenser coil and fan, and charge
Read the alarm on the Intelli-Comfort display / BAS (BACnet values above 128: subtract 128 to get the alarm code); clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list (codes 1-25) as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' (2012) - alarm 1

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 2 locked out due to excessive high pressure switch trips
likelyCauses: Repeated HPS2 trips: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
checks: Check circuit 2 head pressure, condenser coil and fan, and charge; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 2

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 1 locked out due to excessive low pressure switch trips
likelyCauses: Repeated LPS1 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced coil, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 1 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 3

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 2 locked out due to excessive low pressure switch trips
likelyCauses: Repeated LPS2 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced coil, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 2 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 4

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 1 locked out due to excessive freezestat trips
likelyCauses: Evaporator circuit 1 running too cold: low airflow, low charge, low return-air temperature
Failed or miswired freezestat
checks: Inspect the coil for ice; check filters, blower and charge; ohm the freezestat with the coil thawed; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 5

faultCodes.meaning: Compr 2 locked out due to excessive freezestat trips
likelyCauses: Evaporator circuit 2 running too cold: low airflow, low charge, low return-air temperature
Failed or miswired freezestat
checks: Inspect the coil for ice; check filters, blower and charge; ohm the freezestat with the coil thawed; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 6

faultCodes.meaning: Heating locked out due to excessive limit switch trips
likelyCauses: Low airflow across the heat exchanger (filters, blower, dampers, static), overfiring, blower failure
Failed limit switch
checks: Check filters, blower and temperature rise; check manifold pressure; ohm the limit when cool; clear by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 7

faultCodes.meaning: Microelectronics failure, control operating on defaults
likelyCauses: Stored setpoints / configuration corrupted; the control has reverted to factory defaults
Power event or failing board memory
checks: Re-enter the unit configuration and setpoints; cycle power and see whether the alarm returns
Replace the control if it repeats (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 8

faultCodes.meaning: Microelectronics failure, control shut down due to a fatal fault
likelyCauses: Internal control board failure
checks: Cycle power once; if the fatal fault returns, replace the control board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 9

faultCodes.meaning: Control locked out due to fan overload trips
likelyCauses: Supply fan motor overload tripped: high motor amps, wrong pulley setting, bearings, failed overload
Open overload wiring to the control
checks: Check the fan motor overload, motor amps against nameplate and external static; reset and clear the lockout by cycling power after repair (field practice)
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 10

faultCodes.meaning: Control locked out due to low 24 vac
likelyCauses: Low control voltage: transformer undersized or failing, overloaded 24 V circuit, low line voltage, loose connections, high-resistance contactor coils
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the control with contactors energized; check line voltage, transformer tap and total 24 V load
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 11 (alarms 12-18 are listed as not used on Intelli-Comfort)

faultCodes.meaning: Space temperature sensor has failed open
likelyCauses: Open space sensor or sensor wiring; sensor not installed but enabled in configuration
checks: Ohm the space sensor and its wiring at the control; check the configuration if no space sensor is used
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 19

faultCodes.meaning: Supply air temperature sensor has failed open
likelyCauses: Open supply air temperature sensor or wiring; sensor unplugged
checks: Ohm the SAT sensor against a thermometer reading and check its plug and wiring to the control
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 20

faultCodes.meaning: Return air temperature sensor has failed open
likelyCauses: Open return air temperature sensor or wiring; sensor unplugged
checks: Ohm the RAT sensor against a thermometer reading and check its plug and wiring to the control
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 21

faultCodes.meaning: Outside air temperature sensor has failed open
likelyCauses: Open outdoor air temperature sensor or wiring (weather-exposed lead damage), sensor unplugged
checks: Ohm the OAT sensor against a thermometer reading and check its lead and plug; economizer and low-ambient functions depend on it
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 22

faultCodes.meaning: Dirty filter switch tripped
likelyCauses: Filter pressure drop above the field-installed dirty filter switch setpoint (loaded filters)
Switch setpoint too low, tubing reversed or blocked, or switch fitted but filters removed
checks: Replace the filters and confirm the alarm clears; check the switch setpoint and tubing against the filter pressure drop with a manometer
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 23

faultCodes.meaning: Air proving switch open
likelyCauses: Supply fan not producing airflow (motor, belt, VFD), air-proving switch tubing blocked or reversed, or the switch failed
Switch enabled in configuration but not installed
checks: Confirm the supply fan runs and moves air; check the air-proving switch tubing and setpoint with a manometer; check the configuration if no switch is fitted
faultCodes.source: York Intelli-Comfort alarm list as reproduced in HVAC-Talk 'York Bacnet Alarm Values' - alarm 24 (alarm 25 was truncated in the source and is not included)

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number one locked out on High Pressure Control
likelyCauses: HPS1 trips on the 25-40 t Millennium: dirty or blocked condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
Intermittent HPS1 wiring
checks: Check circuit 1 head pressure, condenser coil and fans, and charge
Read the alarm through the Simplicity Elite display / Millennium interface; clear per the manual's Troubleshooting a Millennium section after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 1

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number two locked out on High Pressure Control
likelyCauses: HPS2 trips: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
checks: Check circuit 2 head pressure, condenser coil and fans, and charge; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 2

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number three locked out on High Pressure Control
likelyCauses: HPS3 trips: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
checks: Check circuit 3 head pressure, condenser coil and fans, and charge; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 3

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number four locked out on High Pressure Control
likelyCauses: HPS4 trips: dirty condenser coil, condenser fan failure, overcharge, non-condensables, restriction
checks: Check circuit 4 head pressure, condenser coil and fans, and charge; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 4

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number one locked out on Low Pressure Control
likelyCauses: LPS1 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 1 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 5

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number two locked out on Low Pressure Control
likelyCauses: LPS2 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 2 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 6

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number three locked out on Low Pressure Control
likelyCauses: LPS3 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 3 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 7

faultCodes.meaning: Compressor number four locked out on Low Pressure Control
likelyCauses: LPS4 trips: low charge / leak, restriction, low airflow, iced evaporator, low ambient
checks: Check circuit 4 suction pressure, superheat/subcooling, airflow and leaks; clear after repair
faultCodes.source: York Millennium Simplicity Elite Series Technical Application and Programming Manual 351579-YTS Table 13 'Alarm Default Codes' (p.42) - code 8 (Table 13 continues to code 43 - sensor failures for SAT/RAT/OAT/IAQ/space/RH and duct static / building pressure - which were not readable and are not transcribed)

ledPatterns.meaning: Control Failure - Replace Control (Simplicity / Simplicity LITE UCB)
checks: Verify 24 VAC and the board fuse, cycle power once, then replace the board if it stays steady

ledPatterns.pattern: UCB LED: heartbeat (1 s on / 1 s off)
checks: No fault stored; fault codes are distinguished by a fast ~200 ms on / 200 ms off flash counted between pauses

ledPatterns.meaning: No Power or Control Failure (Simplicity / Simplicity LITE UCB)
checks: Check 24 VAC at the board, transformer secondary and board fuse; replace the board if powered with no LED

ledPatterns.pattern: UCB LED: N fast flashes then pause
ledPatterns.meaning: Fault code N - see the '1 flash' through '14 flashes' entries (Simplicity / Simplicity LITE UCB)
checks: Count flashes between pauses; on original Simplicity boards press LAST ERROR once to replay the last five codes (most recent first)

ledPatterns.meaning: Normal Operation (ignition control board on gas units)
checks: If the UCB shows 9 flashes but the ICB heartbeats, look at the limit / rollout switches and the heat-section jumper plug

ledPatterns.meaning: Ignition fault N - see the 'ICB 1 flash' through 'ICB 10 flashes' entries
checks: Read the ICB LED whenever the UCB shows 9 flashes

ledPatterns.pattern: SE UCB green POWER LED: on
ledPatterns.meaning: 24 VAC present at the C and 24V terminals (display backlight also lit) - Simplicity SE / Smart Equipment UCB
checks: If off, check 24 VAC at the board C/24V terminals, transformer and fuse

ledPatterns.pattern: SE UCB red FAULT LED: flashing during the 90-120 s start-up, then off
ledPatterns.meaning: Normal start-up sequence; the red fault LED lights, goes off briefly, flashes throughout start-up, then stops flashing and turns off - Simplicity SE / Smart Equipment UCB
checks: If it keeps flashing after start-up, read the alarms on the display (Home screen shows up to 5 active alarms) or via SE-MOBILE / MAP Gateway

ledPatterns.pattern: SE UCB green SA BUS LED: flashing
ledPatterns.meaning: UCB has established communication with SA bus devices (economizer, FDD, 4-stage boards) - Simplicity SE / Smart Equipment UCB
checks: Normal; a device that still shows Offline has an addressing or wiring problem on its own leg

ledPatterns.pattern: SE UCB green SA BUS LED: steady on
ledPatterns.meaning: UCB has not established communication and is awaiting communication from SA bus devices (about 15 s after power-up) - Simplicity SE / Smart Equipment UCB
checks: Check SA bus wiring, connectors and power to the economizer / FDD / 4-stage boards; expect the 'Economizer board Offline' type service alarm

diagnosticTips: The flash-code LED is on the unit control board in the control compartment; codes are counted as flashes between pauses.

Original Simplicity boards: press and release the LAST ERROR button once (within 5 s) and the LED replays the last five stored fault codes, most recent first; history is also readable over the Modbus/BAS port.

The complete flash-code table (and the separate Ignition Control Board flash codes on gas units) is printed in the unit installation manual, e.g. ZE036 IOM 5188235-YIM-B-1016 p.66 'Simplicity Lite Unit Control Board Flash Codes / Ignition Control Board Flash Codes', and on the label inside the control box.
Most lockouts clear by removing the thermostat call (or cycling 24 V control power) once the cause is corrected.

Original Simplicity and Simplicity LITE boards: the single flash-code LED is on the UCB in the control compartment. Normal operation is a 1 s on / 1 s off heartbeat; fault codes flash fast (about 200 ms on / 200 ms off) and are counted between pauses. The same numbering (2 = ASCD ... 14 = EEPROM) is used on original Simplicity (Sunline 2000 / Predator, BP/DM IOMs) and Simplicity LITE (ZE/ZF/ZJ Sun Pro IOMs); 3-5 t single-compressor LITE tables omit the HPS2/LPS2/FS2 and fan-overload rows.

Original Simplicity boards (Sunline 2000 / Predator): press and release the LAST ERROR button once within five seconds and the LED flashes the last five stored codes, most recent first; press and release it twice within five seconds to clear the fault history. Fault history is also available over the Modbus/BAS port (York Wireless monitoring / BAS).

Gas units carry a separate ignition control board (ICB) with its own LED; a UCB 9-flash code means go read the ICB LED (2 = pressure switch open, 3 = pressure switch closed, 5 = flame-loss lockout, 6 = limit open, 7 = rollout open, 8 = flame with gas off, 9 = gas valve, 10 = flame-sense circuit).

Most Simplicity / LITE lockouts clear by removing the thermostat call (Y or W) or cycling 24 V control power after the cause is corrected; York Central Tech Talk notes the flash code reports the symptom, not the root cause.

Simplicity SE / Smart Equipment UCB: the board has a 2-line LCD, joystick, ENTER and CANCEL buttons; the Home screen shows the unit mode and up to 5 active alarms. From Home, joystick down to reach the Status / Alarms page; repeatedly pressing CANCEL returns to the Status/Alarms screen. Alarms are grouped as critical (lockouts / shutdowns), service priority and service. The same alarms are available through a network sensor, thermostat X output, the MAP Gateway browser interface, SE-MOBILE (Bluetooth app on newer boards) and BACnet/Modbus/N2 integration.

Simplicity SE hard-lockout reset (firmware 3.3-3.4, York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout' sheet): from IDLE joystick down to Summary > ENTER, down to Sensors > ENTER, down to Unit > ENTER, down to ResetLO > ENTER, move the joystick right until OFF changes to ON, press ENTER and wait for it to return to OFF. Lockouts can also be broken by cycling power. Lockout rules: high pressure 3 trips in 2 h, low pressure 3 trips in 1 h, coil freeze 3 trips in 2 h, limit switch 3 trips in 1 h, air pressure switch (APS) 3 trips in 1.5 h. On firmware 4.0 use the Board Navigation and New Board Setup 4.0 sheet (York Tech Corner) for the menu path.

Simplicity SE start-up: the red FAULT LED flashes throughout the 90-120 s start-up and then turns off; the green SA BUS LED flashes once the UCB is talking to its SA bus boards. A FAULT LED still flashing after start-up means an alarm is active - read it on the display.

Simplicity SE economizer / Title 24 FDD faults (air temperature sensor failure, not economizing when it should, economizing when it should not, damper not modulating, excess outdoor air) are reported on the local LCD, on an NS-series network sensor with fault-code display, via the thermostat X terminal, or through the MAP Gateway.

Intelli-Comfort / Simplicity Elite (D-series 15-25 t and Millennium 25-40 t): alarms are numbered and shown on the controller display or over BACnet/Modbus; on BACnet, alarm values above 128 are the alarm code plus 128 (subtract 128). Millennium Simplicity Elite Table 13 runs to code 43; only codes 1-8 were readable in this pass.

controls.name: Johnson Controls Smart Equipment (Simplicity SE) controller - SE-SPU1001/1002/1011/1012
controls.description: Microprocessor unit controller with on-board LCD and joystick (SE-SPU), optional SE-Mobile app / Verasys BAS; alarms are named text alarms (service and FDD alarms), not numeric codes. Fitted to York/Coleman/Luxaire Z-series and later rooftops from about 2014. Smart Equipment alarm table NOT transcribed: the enrichment run for this platform had no working source access (WebSearch budget exhausted before the agent started; WebFetch/curl blocked; no cached LIT-12011998 / LIT-12011950 / Verasys alarm-summary material on disk). Per the verification protocol no alarm meanings were added from memory. The existing four paraphrased entries remain LOW confidence / 'inferred' and must be verified or replaced from the LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix (Service alarms, FDD alarms) and the Verasys Alarms Summary Technical Bulletin in a follow-up run. Smart Equipment alarms are text alarms on the LCD / app / BAS, not numeric codes or flash codes; the older Simplicity / Simplicity Lite UCB flash codes (e.g. 4 flashes HPS1 lockout) belong to the separate simplicity-ucb platform, not to SE. Transcription status: the critical-alarm rows (HPS1-4, LPS1-4, FS1-4, LS1-3, APS, smoke shutdown, economizer offline) and the five FDD alarm names were seen in manufacturer sources via search summaries of LIT-12011998 / LIT-12011950 / the ZJ IOM alarm table and the SE product bulletin. faultCodes.code: HPS1 / HPS2 / HPS3 / HPS4 lockout (High Pressure Switch, critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm: 'Three HPS1 trips within two hours' (likewise 'Three HPS2 trips within two hours', HPS3, HPS4) - the high-pressure switch of that compressor stage opened three times inside a two-hour window and the control locks out that stage.
likelyCauses: Condenser fan not running (motor, capacitor, contactor, CF output) or condenser coil dirty / airflow blocked
Refrigerant overcharge or non-condensables in the circuit
High outdoor ambient with restricted condenser air, recirculation of discharge air
Failed or miswired HPS (switch open with normal head pressure)
checks: Source: a single HPS trip shows as 'shutdown due to a safety' (circuit open now); three trips in two hours become 'Locked out due to a safety' and need ResetLO or a power cycle after repair (York Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout doc)
Field practice: gauge head pressure against outdoor ambient; verify condenser fan(s) run and the coil is clean
Field practice: with pressures normal, ohm the HPS and its wiring to the UCB HPS input; the safeties override commissioning/test mode, so a tripped HPS also blocks the stage in test (LIT-12011950)
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11; York 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later'

faultCodes.code: LPS1 / LPS2 / LPS3 / LPS4 lockout (Low Pressure Switch, critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm: 'Three LPS1 trips within one hour' (likewise LPS2, LPS3, LPS4) - the low-pressure switch of that compressor stage opened three times inside a one-hour window and the control locks out that stage.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow (dirty filters, slipping belt, closed dampers, dirty coil) causing low suction pressure
Restricted metering device or liquid-line drier
Failed LPS or open wiring; low ambient cooling without low-ambient controls
checks: Source: a single trip reads as 'shutdown due to a safety'; the third trip inside one hour locks the stage out until ResetLO / power cycle (York Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout doc)
Field practice: gauge suction pressure and superheat against the LPS trip point; check evaporator airflow, filters and belt first
Field practice: ohm the LPS with the circuit equalized and inspect the LPS wiring to the UCB input
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11 and 'Unit protection / Low pressure switch'

faultCodes.code: FS1 / FS2 / FS3 / FS4 lockout (Freeze Switch / freezestat, critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm: 'Three FS1 trips within two hours' (likewise FS2, FS3, FS4) - the freezestat of that compressor stage opened three times inside a two-hour window and the control locks out that stage.
likelyCauses: Low evaporator airflow (filters, belt, blower speed, closed dampers) letting the coil frost
Low refrigerant charge
Freezestat sensing bulb loose or misplaced on the coil, or failed freezestat
Cooling running at low return-air temperature (economizer / low load) without low-ambient provisions
checks: Secondary (HVAC-Talk, York rooftop): the freeze stat opens at about 26 F coil temperature and closes at about 41 F; three trips in a two-hour window lock out that compressor stage (CR1 / CR2)
Field practice: measure evaporator airflow / static pressure, suction pressure and superheat while the coil is clear
Field practice: verify the freezestat is mounted on the coil correctly and check its continuity with the coil above the reset point; clear the lockout with ResetLO or a power cycle after repair
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11 and 'Unit protection / Freezestat alarm'

faultCodes.code: LS1 / LS2 / LS3 lockout (gas heat Limit Switch, critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm: 'Three LS1 trips within one hour' (likewise LS2, LS3) - the heat-section limit switch of that heating stage opened three times inside a one-hour window and the control locks out that heating stage.
likelyCauses: Insufficient airflow across the heat exchanger (dirty filters, belt, blower speed, blocked supply/return)
Over-fired burner (gas pressure / manifold pressure too high) or wrong orifice
Restricted heat exchanger or flue; failed or weak limit switch
Fan-on-heat delay / blower not running while burner is on
checks: Source: the UCB monitors the MV (gas valve) input and starts the FAN ON HEAT DELAY timer when 24 V appears on MV; heating stages are H1-H3 (LIT-12011950 gas heating sequence)
Field practice: verify blower runs during heat, measure temperature rise against the nameplate range and check manifold gas pressure
Field practice: ohm the limit switch cold and inspect the LS wiring to the UCB; clear the lockout with ResetLO or a power cycle after repair
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11

faultCodes.code: APS lockout (Air Proving Switch, critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm: 'Three APS trips within 1.5 hours' - the supply-fan air proving input (SF_APS, 'the feedback from the Air Proven Switch or a current sensor') was lost three times inside a 1.5-hour window; 'Supply Fan is required before allowing compressor and heat stage outputs', so cooling and heating are held off.
likelyCauses: Supply fan not running (belt broken, motor overload, contactor, VFD fault) or fan running backwards
APS differential switch tubing disconnected/kinked, switch failed or set too tight; current sensor not seeing motor current
Extremely dirty filters or blocked ductwork dropping the fan differential below the switch setting
checks: Source: the Supply fan status screen shows SF On and the UO9 light On when the fan output is energized; APS status is shown on the same status screens (LIT-12011950 Air proving switch setup / Operation)
Field practice: with the fan commanded on, confirm rotation, belt and motor amps, then jumper/measure the APS input to separate a fan problem from a switch problem
Field practice: check APS tubing and setting; clear the lockout with ResetLO or a power cycle once the fan proves
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation 'Air proving switch setup'

faultCodes.code: Unit Shutdown Due to Smoke (critical alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Critical alarm 'Unit Shutdown Due to Smoke': raised when 'the SD input loses 24 VAC' - the smoke-detector / shutdown input circuit to the UCB has opened and the unit shuts down.
likelyCauses: Duct smoke detector tripped (real smoke or a dirty/over-sensitive detector)
Field shutdown / fire-alarm relay contact opened, or SD jumper removed on a unit without a detector
Broken wire or loose terminal in the SD 24 VAC loop
checks: Field practice: measure 24 VAC at the UCB SD input; trace the loop through the duct detector(s) and any fire-alarm interlock relay
Field practice: reset the duct detector and check its sensitivity / cleanliness; confirm the factory jumper is present when no detector is installed
Source: critical alarms need ResetLO or a power cycle to restore operation after the cause is repaired (York Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout doc)
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2 (Critical alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11

faultCodes.code: Economizer board goes from Online to Offline (SA bus communication alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Alarm 'Economizer board goes from Online to Offline' - the UCB lost SA-bus communication with the SE-ECO economizer controller that it had previously discovered.
likelyCauses: 24 VAC power lost at the economizer board (24V~ IN COM / HOT)
SA bus cable unplugged, reversed polarity or wrong addressing between UCB and economizer board
Economizer board firmware error or failed board
checks: Source: the economizer board power LED lit = 24 VAC present; a 1/10-second on/off flash = networking error (polarity, addressing) or firmware error (reload from USB); SA bus LED lit/flickering = UCB-to-economizer SA bus communication active, off = board awaiting SA bus communication (SE-ECO1001-1 catalog page)
Source: the UCB green SA bus LED flashes when the UCB has established communication with SA bus devices (Quick Start Guide LIT-12011938)
Field practice: reseat/replace the SA bus cable, check 24 VAC at the board, then run RELEARN so the UCB rediscovers connected boards
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix Table 2; LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Table 11 (non-FDD alarms); SE-ECO1001-1 catalog page (LEDs)

faultCodes.code: Shutdown due to a safety (single HPS / LPS / FS / LS / APS trip, service priority alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Service priority fault: the alarm text reads 'shutdown due to a safety' rather than 'Locked out due to a safety'. 'If the alarm says shutdown, it means the circuit is open at that time.' Service Priority Faults 'shut down a portion of the unit operation and count toward maximum shutdowns prior to lockout'; they 'clear themselves once the problem is corrected or the safety resets'.
likelyCauses: The named safety switch (HPS, LPS, freezestat, limit, air proving) is currently open - see the matching lockout entry for causes
Intermittent wiring at the switch or UCB input
checks: Source: the affected stage restarts by itself when the switch closes; three trips inside the window (HPS/FS two hours, LPS/LS one hour, APS 1.5 hours) escalate to the critical lockout alarm
Field practice: read the alarm while the switch is still open and measure the switch input to identify which safety is open before it resets
faultCodes.source: York Tech Corner 'Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout Ver 3.3 or later' (alarm categories); LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 2 (Service priority alarms)

faultCodes.code: Excessive Supply Air Temp Cooling (supply-air temperature limit)
faultCodes.meaning: 'YORK units have a secondary safety built into the SE control that monitors supply air temperature and will drop stages of cooling or heat if the supply temperature exceeds the setting in the SE control. As the supply temperature returns to within the limitations, stages of heat or cool will be allowed to restart after any anti short cycle timers have expired.' The 'Excessive Supply Air Temp Cooling' alarm is one of the alarms that prevents cooling operation.
likelyCauses: Cooling SAT limit reached (default 45 F, adjustable down to 40 F): low airflow, low load, economizer plus mechanical cooling, or oversized staging
Heating counterpart: SAT above the heating limit (default 140 F, adjustable to 180 F) from low airflow or over-firing
Supply air sensor misplaced (too close to coil / heat exchanger) or reading wrong
checks: Source: limits are set under Details > Cooling > Setup and Details > Heating > Setup; the safety can be disabled in the SE control (York 'Excessive Supply Temperature')
Field practice: verify airflow (filters, belt, blower speed, static) and compare the SAT reading with a reference thermometer in the supply duct
Field practice: on VAV units also review low-limit tempering setpoints (LL_LOWSAT_SP default 65 F, LL_UPSAT_SP default 80 F) before raising the limit
faultCodes.source: York Tech Corner 'Excessive Supply Temperature' (Rev1 01092020); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation (low limit tempering setpoints)

faultCodes.code: Space temperature cooling alarm / Space temperature heating alarm (service alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: Space temperature cooling alarm: the space temperature exceeds the operating cooling setpoint for more than 60 minutes. Space temperature heating alarm: the space temperature is less than the operating heating setpoint for more than 60 minutes.
likelyCauses: Unit unable to meet load: locked-out or shut-down stages (see safety alarms), low charge, dirty coils/filters
Setpoint or schedule change, wrong occupancy source, or space sensor reading wrong / badly located
Excessive outdoor air (economizer stuck open) or building load beyond capacity
checks: Source: this is an informative service alarm - it does not itself shut the unit down (alarm categories per York Alarm Reset / Hard Lockout doc)
Field practice: check the active alarms list for a safety lockout first, then compare space temperature, setpoints and stage status on the UCB Status screens
Field practice: verify the space / network sensor reading against a reference thermometer
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011950 Smart Equipment Controls Sequence of Operation Technical Bulletin 5.0, 'Space temperature alarming'; LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix (Service alarms)

faultCodes.meaning: FDD alarm 'Air Temp Sensor Fault' indicates a problem with one of the air temperature sensors; check the Outdoor Air, Return Air or Supply Air sensors. The FDD also reports a fault when the local supply air temperature (SAT) sensor is disconnected from the unit controller.
likelyCauses: OAT, RAT or SAT sensor unplugged, open, shorted or corroded connector
Sensor reading implausible (mounted in sun, in the discharge stream, or in a dead pocket)
'Phantom' alarm: the sensor is not installed on this unit but its input is still enabled (see Phantom entry)
checks: Field practice: scroll the Status screens (joystick down through SAT, RAT, OAT) and compare each reading with a reference thermometer; ohm the 10k thermistor against the resistance table in the SE technical guide
Source: economizing is not performed when the SAT is unreliable and the unit is configured for zone control or demand air temperature control (LIT-12011950)
Source: FDD faults can be viewed on the UCB local display, the network sensor, a thermostat with the X (fault) output, the MAP gateway or the BAS (SEC Product Bulletin)
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 3 (FDD alarms); Smart Equipment Controls (SEC) Product Bulletin LIT-12011934 (economizer FDD); JCI Title 24 Impact on Packaged Rooftop Units Application Guide

faultCodes.code: Not Economizing When It Should (FDD alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: FDD alarm 'Not Economizing When It Should' - the economizer is not using outdoor air when it should (outdoor conditions are suitable for free cooling but the damper is not opening).
likelyCauses: Damper actuator failed, linkage disconnected or damper stuck closed
Changeover setpoint / enthalpy or dry-bulb settings too restrictive; economizer disabled in setup
OAT / RAT (or humidity) sensor reading wrong so the control believes free cooling is unavailable
checks: Field practice: command the damper in test/commissioning mode and watch actuator travel; check 24 VAC and the control signal at the actuator
Field practice: verify the economizer changeover method and setpoints under Details > Economizer, and the OAT/RAT readings

Source: FDD alarms and economizer sensor fault indications can be enabled or disabled from the display (LIT-12011950 'Disable or Enable FDD Alarms' / 'Disable or Enable Economizer Sensor Fault Indications')
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 3 (FDD alarms); LIT-12011950 Table 12 (FDD alarms); JCI Title 24 Impact on Packaged Rooftop Units Application Guide

faultCodes.code: Economizing When It Should Not (FDD alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: FDD alarm 'Economizing When It Should Not' ('economizing when not required') - the economizer is bringing in outdoor air for cooling when outdoor conditions are not suitable.
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open or actuator not closing (linkage, failed actuator, loss of control signal)
Changeover setpoints set too high / wrong changeover method for the climate
OAT or RAT sensor error making outdoor air look cooler than it is
checks: Field practice: verify damper closes to minimum position when commanded; check actuator feedback and linkage
Field practice: compare OAT/RAT readings and the changeover setpoint; correct sensor placement
Source: FDD faults are reported on the UCB display, network sensor, thermostat X output, MAP gateway or BAS (SEC Product Bulletin)
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 3 (FDD alarms); LIT-12011950 Table 12 (FDD alarms); JCI Title 24 Impact on Packaged Rooftop Units Application Guide

faultCodes.meaning: FDD alarm 'Damper Not Modulating' - the economizer damper is not able to modulate properly; check the damper, the linkage to the actuator, or the actuator.
likelyCauses: Actuator failed, no 24 VAC, or control signal missing / wrong (2-10 V)
Linkage slipped, damper blades seized or obstructed
Actuator feedback wiring open so the control cannot confirm position
checks: Field practice: drive the damper open and closed from the commissioning / test menu and watch for movement and feedback change
Field practice: check actuator power, signal and feedback at the economizer board terminals; free up or replace the damper linkage
Field practice: re-run the economizer commissioning after repair and confirm the FDD alarm clears
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 3 (FDD alarms); LIT-12011950 Table 12 (FDD alarms); JCI Title 24 Impact on Packaged Rooftop Units Application Guide

faultCodes.meaning: FDD alarm 'Excess Outdoor Air' - the economizer is allowing excess outdoor air inside (more than the minimum position / ventilation requirement calls for).
likelyCauses: Minimum position set too high or damper not returning to minimum (actuator, linkage, feedback)
Damper blade seals damaged, damper stuck partly open
Return-air damper / hood problems, or OAT/RAT/SAT sensor error skewing the outdoor-air fraction calculation
checks: Field practice: verify minimum position setting and actual damper position at minimum; inspect blade seals and linkage
Field practice: check the OAT, RAT and SAT readings the control uses to estimate outdoor-air fraction
Source: FDD alarms can be disabled/enabled from the display if the ventilation design intentionally exceeds the default expectations (LIT-12011950)
faultCodes.source: LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 3 (FDD alarms); LIT-12011950 Table 12 (FDD alarms); JCI Title 24 Impact on Packaged Rooftop Units Application Guide

faultCodes.code: Phantom sensor / economizer alarm (sensor not installed)
faultCodes.meaning: 'Phantom Alarms' are active alarms displayed that represent failures of sensors that are physically not installed on the unit (typically economizer / accessory sensor fault indications).
likelyCauses: Board replaced or reconfigured with sensor/accessory inputs enabled that the unit does not have
Accessory board or sensor removed after the UCB had discovered it
Sensor fault indications left enabled for optional economizer sensors
