diagnosticTips: Use the SE-SPU's LCD and joystick (Alarms menu) or the SE-Mobile app / Verasys UI to read active and historical alarms; the alarm names are text, not numeric codes.

The verbatim alarm tables are in the Smart Equipment Controls Technical Bulletin LIT-12011998 (Alarm appendix: Service alarms and FDD alarms) and the Simplicity SE Controls Technical Guide (SE-SPU1001/1002/1011/1012); the 2-stage rooftop guide is 5127914-UTG-B-1116.
Verasys Alarms Summary Technical Bulletin (Smart Equipment RTU controller section) lists the same alarms as seen from the BAS.
Compressor lockouts are cleared from the Alarms / Details menu or by cycling power once the cause is corrected.

Display: the UCB (SE-SPU) has an on-board LCD with a joystick, ENTER and CANCEL buttons. Move the joystick up/down to scroll menu items and press ENTER to open a sub-menu or show a property value; press CANCEL repeatedly to return to the IDLE (home) screen. Joystick down from IDLE scrolls SAT, RAT, OAT and the other sensor readings (Status).

Alarms: 'Alarms' is a top-level menu on the UCB display; the home screen can display up to 5 active alarms. Alarms are grouped as critical, service priority and service (LIT-12011998 Alarm appendix Table 2); FDD alarms are a separate table (Table 3). The same alarms are visible through the SE-Mobile app / MAP gateway, a network sensor, a thermostat with the X fault output, or the BAS (Verasys / Metasys).

Reading alarm text: 'shutdown due to a safety' means the safety circuit is open right now (service priority - auto-clears when the safety resets and counts toward the maximum shutdowns before lockout); 'Locked out due to a safety' is a critical alarm (three trips in the window) that stays until reset.

Clearing a hard lockout (ResetLO): firmware 1.0-3.2: Details > Unit > ResetLO. Firmware 3.3-3.4: from IDLE joystick down to Summary > ENTER > Sensors > ENTER > Unit > ENTER > ResetLO > ENTER. Later firmware: Summary > Unit > ResetLO. Push the joystick right to change OFF to ON and press ENTER; after 3-5 seconds ON changes back to OFF on its own, which means the reset is complete and the lockout is broken. Cycling unit power also clears critical lockouts. If the lockout does not reset, the fault still exists.

RELEARN (make the UCB rediscover connected boards/sensors, clears phantom sensor alarms): firmware 1.0-3.2: from IDLE joystick down to Controller > ENTER > SysCntlrs > ENTER > Misc > ENTER > RELEARN > ENTER (display shows False/True). Perform it with the unit not operating; on 3.3+ the ResetLO function performs the equivalent.

FDD: economizer FDD is built into the standard software and is enabled in the field from the unit keypad/display; FDD alarms and economizer sensor fault indications can be disabled/enabled from the display (LIT-12011950 Alarms section). FDD faults can be read on the UCB display, MAP gateway or BAS.

Supply-air limits: the SE control drops cooling/heating stages when SAT exceeds the cooling limit (default 45 F, adjustable to 40 F) or heating limit (default 140 F, adjustable to 180 F); set under Details > Cooling > Setup and Details > Heating > Setup.

Safeties override commissioning/test mode: a compressor cannot be energized in test if its HPS is tripped. The supply fan must be proven (APS / current sensor input) before compressor and heat outputs are allowed.

Verbatim alarm tables: LIT-12011998 Smart Equipment Control Technical Bulletin, Alarm appendix (Critical alarms, Service priority alarms, Service alarms, FDD alarms); LIT-12011950 Sequence of Operation Overview, Alarms (Table 11 non-FDD alarms, Table 12 FDD alarms); Verasys Alarms Summary Technical Bulletin, 'Smart Equipment Rooftop Unit (RTU) Controller' section (BAS view of the same alarms).

ledPatterns.meaning: Active fault(s) present on the control board (for example sensors or options that are not installed or are disconnected).

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling: thermostat Y1 (and G) to the UCB -> after any anti-short-cycle delay the board energizes compressor contactor 1M and the condenser fan(s); the indoor blower runs on G (or after a short delay on the board). Y2 adds circuit 2 (2M). Economizer, when enabled and outdoor air suitable, is used as first-stage cooling before compressors.

Gas heating: W1 to the UCB -> ignition control (IGC) energizes the combustion-air motor, proves the pressure switch, runs the ignition trial, opens the gas valve; the indoor blower starts after the heat blower-on delay. W2 brings on high fire / second heat section. Limit or rollout opening drops the gas valve; rollout is manual reset.

Safety: an HPS/LPS/freeze-stat opening drops that circuit's contactor; repeated trips within one call cause a board lockout indicated by the LED flash code (Simplicity) or a named alarm (Smart Equipment).

commonIssues.symptom: Unit dead or erratic - LED steady on / no heartbeat (Sunline 2000 / Predator with original Simplicity board)
likelyCauses: Failed original Simplicity control board (well-known field failure on 1998-2009 D-series units)
Blown board fuse from a shorted 24 V field wire
Transformer failure
checks: Verify 24 VAC at R-C and the board fuse
Check for a shorted thermostat cable or economizer wiring before replacing the board
If steady-on LED persists with good supply, replace the UCB (retrofit kits exist)

commonIssues.symptom: Compressors will not run in cool weather; flash code 10 on the board
likelyCauses: Low ambient switch closed (normal below ~45 F)
Failed low ambient switch
checks: Note outdoor ambient; above 55 F the switch should be open
Ohm the LAS and its wiring to the UCB

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat lockout / no ignition on rooftop
likelyCauses: Combustion-air pressure switch not proving (blocked flue, failed inducer/combustion motor, cracked hose)
Dirty flame sensor
Rollout switch tripped (manual reset) from heat-exchanger or burner problems
Gas valve or supply pressure problem

Check inlet/manifold gas pressure

Clean the flame sensor and check the microamp signal
Inspect the heat exchanger if rollout has tripped

commonIssues.symptom: Low pressure / freeze lockouts on Z-series or SE-controlled units
likelyCauses: Dirty filters or slipping/broken blower belt (low airflow)

Suction pressure and superheat
Economizer minimum position and actuator operation

commonIssues.symptom: Smart Equipment unit runs but not to setpoint; sensor alarms on SE-SPU

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not modulating / free cooling never used
likelyCauses: Failed actuator or economizer logic module
